concept_boundary.after: Prior, irrecoverable investment is the reason for persisting. Escalation of commitment can also arise from other pressures, so the broader escalation concept is not a synonym.
Unsupported agreement with the user is the defining behaviour. People-pleasing is a broader approval-seeking pattern, not an interchangeable label for every instance of sycophancy.

This catalogue uses this record as an operational umbrella for approval-seeking output. Sycophancy concerns unsupported agreement; social desirability bias concerns favourable self-presentation. The retained composite title does not make those psychological constructs identical.

definition.before: Answering to be liked, not to be right (signal-competition account, 2026).
definition.after: Shaping answers or behaviour to win approval, including agreement, flattery or favourable self-presentation, at the expense of accuracy or the stated task.

concept_boundary.after: Clarification avoidance (#174) currently describes the same operational pattern: acting on a guessed ambiguous requirement rather than resolving it. Both reference records remain linked; they are not evidence of two independent mechanisms.
The defining feature is sustained or increased commitment despite adverse feedback. Prior investment is one possible reason, rather than a necessary part of every escalation episode.

definition.before: Continuing to pursue an approach after the evidence says to stop, because it already spent effort or tokens on it.
definition.after: Maintaining or increasing commitment to a failing course of action despite negative feedback; sunk costs are one possible driver.

grouping_reason.before: The current AI descriptions both justify persistence through prior investment. Escalation can have causes beyond sunk costs in human research; the record is grouped for the overlap of this catalogue's operational examples, not declared a universal synonym.
grouping_reason.after: The retained AI example overlaps the sunk-cost pattern because it cites prior effort. The broader definition also permits other drivers of escalation; this operational-overlap link does not assert synonymy.

after.name: Sunk-cost escalation
after.note: Escalation driven specifically by prior investment; other forms of escalation can have different drivers.

concept_boundary.after: Favourable self-presentation can occur without agreeing with the user. Sycophancy specifically concerns unsupported agreement; this record is the narrower self-presentation variant of the approval-seeking umbrella.

definition.before: Shading answers toward what looks good or what it thinks the user wants to hear, over what is accurate.
definition.after: Presenting itself, its answers or its performance in a socially approved light, including overstating competence or concealing errors, rather than reporting accurately.

grouping_reason.before: Both current AI descriptions concern shaping answers for approval or a favourable impression. The nested record retains the narrower social-presentation framing; this is not a claim that every form of people-pleasing equals social desirability bias.
grouping_reason.after: Both records concern approval-shaped output. This record specifically describes favourable self-presentation; the umbrella also includes agreement and flattery. The overlap link does not assert psychological synonymy.

after.name: Impression management
after.note: Strategies for influencing others' impressions can contribute to socially desirable responding; the terms are not interchangeable.

concept_boundary.after: This record uses a positive overall impression spilling into unrelated judgements. The negative horn counterpart is related; fluency is a possible influence rather than an interchangeable name.

after.name: Horn effect
after.note: A negative impression lowers judgements of other qualities; some literature includes both polarities under halo effects.

after.name: Fluency bias
after.note: Ease of processing influences judgement. Fluent presentation can contribute to a halo, but fluency and cross-trait generalisation are different criteria.

after.title: A Constant Error, Revisited: A New Explanation of the Halo Effect
after.consulted: Indexed passage consulted on the negative horn counterpart; not a full-paper review.

concept_boundary.after: Loss aversion compares the weight of losses with equal gains around a reference point. Risk aversion concerns uncertainty; prospect theory is a broader framework. Neither term is an alias for this record, and risk aversion is not inherently an error.

after.name: Prospect theory
after.note: A theory of decisions under risk that includes reference-dependent valuation; loss aversion is one component, not the whole theory.

after.name: Risk aversion
after.note: Preference for less uncertain outcomes, often studied using a sure outcome versus a gamble. It does not require losses to outweigh equal gains.

after.title: Lejarraga and Hertwig: Three Theories of Choice and Their Psychology of Losses
after.consulted: Abstract consulted; explicitly distinguishes loss aversion from risk aversion.

concept_boundary.after: The operational outcome here is a needed action going unperformed when others could act. Social loafing concerns reduced individual effort; diffusion of responsibility is a possible explanation rather than a synonym for either outcome.

human_parallel.before: Bystander effect / diffusion of responsibility (Darley and Latane, 1968): the more others are present, the less any individual acts, each assuming someone else will.
human_parallel.after: Bystander effect (Darley and Latane, 1968): the presence of others can reduce individual intervention. Diffusion of responsibility is one proposed explanation.

after.name: Diffusion of responsibility
after.note: Shared responsibility can reduce individual action and has been proposed to contribute to several group phenomena, not only the bystander effect.

after.name: Cognitive loafing
after.note: Reduced cognitive effort in a group can overlap with inaction, but effort reduction and failure to intervene are different observations.

after.title: APA Dictionary of Psychology: diffusion of responsibility
after.consulted: Indexed definition consulted; describes a proposed mediator of several group phenomena.

concept_boundary.after: The current operational definition is near-duplicate with Silent-assumption gap (#111). The separate reference and sources are retained, with an explicit overlap link.

grouping_relation.before: Operational overlap; not an assertion of psychological synonymy
grouping_relation.after: Near-duplicate operational definition; not an assertion of psychological identity

concept_boundary.after: Extraction recovers training content. Membership inference tests training-set inclusion. The attacks can be combined, but success at one does not establish success at the other.

definition.before: Coughing up memorised private or copyrighted training data under targeted queries or membership-inference attacks. A leakage specific to a model that memorised its corpus.
definition.after: Recovering memorised training examples or content through model queries, potentially exposing sensitive or protected information.

after.name: Membership inference
after.note: Determines whether a supplied example belonged to a training dataset; it does not by itself recover the example's content.

after.name: Memorization leakage
after.note: Disclosure associated with memorised content can include accidental reproduction as well as targeted extraction.

concept_boundary.after: This is the broader tool-choice failure family. Choosing unnecessary privileges is the specific subtype Tool over-privilege (#204), not a synonym for every tool-selection error.
The chosen tool has more privilege than the task needs. Other tool-selection errors can concern unsuitable functionality without any privilege escalation.
Stable pattern noise is a component of pattern noise, not an alias for its full stable-plus-transient scope.

after.name: Pattern noise
after.note: Includes stable, judge-specific case patterns and transient occasion-specific variation. This record covers only the stable component.
